questions.text: Let X and Y be nonempty sets and ∼ an arbitrary binary relation. Then briefly explain the following: (i) An injective mapping f : X → Y (1 mark); (ii) A totally ordered set (X, ∼) (4 marks); (iii) Given a subset S of X, a first element of S (2 marks).

Let X = {1, 2, 3, 4}. Consider the relations R₁ = {(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (4,4), (2,3), (3,2), (1,4)} and R₂ = {(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (2,3), (1,2), (2,1), (1,3), (3,1), (4,4)}. (i) Is R₁ an equivalence relation? Justify your answer (1 mark); (ii) Is R₂ an equivalence relation? Justify your answer (3 marks); (iii) Hence, consider a relation ∼ on R² such that for (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂) ∈ R², (x₁, y₁) ∼ (x₂, y₂) ⇔ |x₁ − y₁| = |y₂ − x₂|. Show whether or not ∼ is an equivalence relation (9 marks).

Briefly explain the following: (i) (a, b) = 1 (1 mark); (ii) lcm[a, b] (2 marks); (iii) An integer p a prime number (2 marks); (iv) Hence, find the gcd(945, 2415) = d and integers u and v such that d = 2415u + 945v (8 marks).
(i) State the fundamental theorem of arithmetic (2 marks); (ii) State the Euclidean division algorithm (2 marks); (iii) Find all the solutions of the congruent equation 12x ≡ 3 (mod 9) (2 marks).

Given a nonempty set X, operation + (usual addition) and × (usual multiplication): (i) When is (X, +, ×) said to be a ring? (4 marks) (ii) When is the ring (X, +, ×) said to be an integral domain? (iii) State the Lagrange Theorem (2 marks).

Consider the set Z₈: (i) Find the set Z_φ(8) of all elements x ∈ Z₈ such that (x, 8) = 1 (1 mark); (ii) Compute the totient φ(8) (1 mark); (iii) Construct a Cayley's multiplication table modulo 8 for (Z_φ(8), ×₈) (4 marks); (iv) Justify whether (Z_φ(8), ×₈) is a group or not (5 marks).
Consider the matrix A with rows (1, −3, 3), (3, −5, 3), (6, −6, 4): (i) Find the associated eigenvalues to matrix A (7 marks); (ii) Find the associated diagonal matrix A_D (2 marks).
(i) State Cayley-Hamilton's theorem (2 marks); (ii) Verify Cayley-Hamilton's theorem for the matrix B with rows (4, 1), (3, 2).

Let V be an additive abelian group and F any field of numbers: (i) When is V said to be a vector space over F? (4 marks) (ii) Given a set {v₁, v₂, v₃, …, vₙ} of nonzero vectors in V and a set of scalars {λ₁, λ₂, λ₃, …, λₙ} in F. When is this set of vectors considered to be a basis for V? (2 marks) (iii) Given a field R of real numbers, construct vector space over R and define its typical element, vector addition and scalar multiplication (2 marks); (iv) Show that the nonzero vectors in the vector space V over a field F is linearly dependent if one of the vectors is a linear combination of the others (4 marks).

Consider the mapping T : Vₙ(F) → Vₘ(F) from the n-dimensional vector space to an m-dimensional vector space over the field F: (i) When is T said to be a linear transformation? (2 marks) (ii) What is kernel of T, denoted ker(T)? (1 mark) (iii) Show whether the mapping T : R³ → R³, defined by T(x, y, z) = (x, 0, z), is a linear transformation or not (5 marks).
Let X be a nonempty set. i. What is a partition on X? ii. When is (X, ∼) said to be a partially ordered set?

i. When is ∼ said to be an equivalence relation on X? ii. Hence, let Z be a set of integers a relation ∼ on X be defined by x ∼ y if and only if ∃ m ∈ Z* such that m | (x − y) for every x, y ∈ Z. Show whether or not ∼ is an equivalence relation.
In a truth-value table, show whether or not ¬(p ∨ ¬(p ∧ q)) ≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q. (The bars in the printed paper are faint; the statement is given as best it can be read.)
Let f : X → Y and g : Y → Z be mappings of nonempty sets. Show that if f and g are injective, then g ∘ f is injective.

Let V be a nonempty set and F a field of scalars. i. When is V said to be a vector space over F? ii. When is the set {vᵢ}ⁿᵢ₌₁ of vectors in V said to be linearly independent given that {λᵢ}ⁿᵢ₌₁ is a set of scalars from F? iii. If T : Vₘ → Vₙ is a linear transformation, what is kernel of T? Hence, if f : R³ → R² is a Linear Transformation defined by f(x, y, z) = (x + y, z) ∀ x, y, z ∈ R, compute the kernel of f.

Consider a nonempty set R and binary operations + and × as the usual addition and multiplication of numbers respectively. a. When is R said to be a ring? b. If (R, +, ×) is a ring, is (R, +) an abelian group? Justify your answer. c. When is the ring (R, +, ×) said to be a field? d. Let f : (N, +) → (N, +) be a mapping defined by f(n) = an ∀ n ∈ N and some a ∈ N. Show whether or not f is a monomorphism.

a. State the Euclidean Algorithm. b. Define gcd(a, b) for a, b ∈ Z. c. i. Find the integers d = gcd(33, 280), u and v such that d = 33u + 280v. ii. Hence, solve the congruent equation 33x ≡ 38 (mod 280). d. Compute the totient of Z₁₈.

Consider a matrix A with rows (3, −4), (2, −6). a. Find the eigenvalues of A. b. Find the eigenvectors of A. c. State Caley-Hamilton's theorem. d. Verify Caley-Hamilton's theorem with A. e. Find the diagonal matrix D which is similar to A. f. Find the matrix P such that P⁻¹AP = D.
